summary: discord-mfa 3.0.0 fetches and executes remote Windows payload on require with multi-vector persistence
details: On require('discord-mfa'), lib/cache.js runs an IIFE gated on os.platform() === 'win32' that creates %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\WinSxS\Backup\, downloads a remote JavaScript file from https://limbomail.com/attachment/yl8ulfsxnzrV.p9VNqox-hxFRxKJEnv20ByL1bUqiVp3- to winsvc.js, and spawns it detached via node.exe. lib/totp.js then installs four Windows persistence entries pointing at that dropped script: an HKCU\...\CurrentVersion\Run value named WinSvcHost, an HKCU\Environment UserInitMprLogonScript, a hidden+system wsvc.vbs launcher placed in the user's Startup folder, and a scheduled task \Microsoft\Windows\Shell\WinSvcHost triggered at logon. The remote URL, directory names, child_process module name, execSync/spawn API names, registry paths, schtasks/attrib commands, and target filenames are all hex- or base64-obfuscated while the surrounding MFA-themed code is plaintext. The masquerading names (WinSvcHost, WinSxS\Backup) impersonate legitimate Windows components.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
